summary: Traced ONE reader journey (my bill went up -> why -> what do I do) to the bottom across all 14 assigned pages. findings: Where the journey breaks — TOP 3 breakpoints: (1) net-metering-explained and ev-charging-impact-electric-bill are ABSOLUTE DEAD ENDS: 0 internal links each (rg-confirmed), yet 03 links TO ev-charging and which-rate-plan links TO net-metering, so readers that follow a logical next step fall off a cliff. (2) complete-guide-understanding-utility-bill — the apex hub with 28 ilinks — never links to how-to-dispute-utility-bill, can-utility-shut-off-service, or utility-assistance-programs-liheap; its 'When to escalate safely' section describes a billing-review process without pointing to the site's own dispute page. (3) 03-why-is-my-electric-bill-so-high and why-did-my-utility-bill-go-up-this-month tell the reader to 'contact the utility / dispute' but link none of the act pages, so the diagnose cluster splits without an act exit.

Pages rated below 6/10: how-utility-rates-fees-usage-work-together (Quality 5, SEO 5 — HTML-body structural mismatch, only 1 markdown internal link). Net-metering (SEO 4) and EV-charging (SEO 4) would be below on SEO despite decent content — worst overall search-readiness in the set.

3 highest-impact actions: (A) add internal links from net-metering & ev-charging into which-rate-plan / 08-time-of-use / 46-what-time / 49-demand / electric-bill-breakdown — converts 2 dead ends into onward paths and distributes link equity; (B) add act-cluster edges from complete-guide and 03 to dispute/shutoff/assistance/rate-plan — wires diagnose -> act -> plan; (C) close the crisis loop with dispute -> internal utility-assistance and LIHEAP -> can-utility-shutoff (currently only external liheap.org cited).

Confirmed missing edges (names both endpoints + reader need): complete-guide -> how-to-dispute (pillar hub reader who concludes bill wrong needs the dispute path); 03 -> how-to-dispute / can-utility-shutoff / which-rate-plan (error branch has no act exit); which-rate-plan -> ev-charging (decision list item #1 explicitly mentions EV overnight charging but doesn't link the EV cost page); LIHEAP -> can-utility-shutoff (emergency Day-1 section missing the protections page); dispute -> utility-assistance (payment-assistance section quotes LIHEAP, links external liheap.org only).
